title: Add Support-facing signal to routing fallback metrics (activation + reason)
creator: Mina Haddad
project: Support Escalation Playbook Refresh / Known-Issues Sprint (2026-02)
description:
Support needs a fast, unambiguous way to confirm whether routing fallback is actively occurring (and why) during incidents and escalations.

Today we have partial signals (overall error rate, per-model traffic shifts, some router logs), but nothing that cleanly answers:
- Did fallback routing activate for this route/tenant tier/region?
- What was the reason (capacity, model health, policy override, region failover, version incompatibility)?
- What was requested vs what was served (requested model/version vs served model/version)?

This gap shows up repeatedly in escalations where customers believe pinned model/version is being ignored or where mitigations involve temporarily enabling fallback to keep availability. Support currently has to ask SRE/Platform to confirm via internal tooling/logs, increasing time-to-mitigation and bridge noise.

Scope:
1) Add/clarify router metrics indicating fallback activation, with low-cardinality labels safe for Support dashboards.
2) Provide a Support-friendly dashboard panel and a short runbook snippet: “How to confirm fallback is happening + how to interpret reasons.”

Non-goals:
- Do not add high-cardinality labels (customer_id, request_id, prompt hash).
- Do not expose customer-identifying data in metrics.
- Do not replace existing incident process; this is a triage accelerant, not a new paging trigger (paging remains per SRE policy).
acceptance_criteria:
- A new counter exists for fallback activation events and is queryable in the standard metrics backend.
- Metric includes labels sufficient for Support triage: region, route, customer_tier, requested_model, served_model, reason.
- Reason labels are a constrained enum (documented) with <10 values.
- A dashboard panel exists in the “Support Quick View” set showing fallback rate (%) over time by region/route and top reasons.
- Runbook snippet added (or linked) describing: definitions, common reasons, and when Support should escalate to SRE/Platform.
- Verified in staging and one production region via canary that metrics increment as expected when fallback is forced.
- No unacceptable cardinality increase (validated with metrics review checklist).
implementation_notes:
Proposed metrics (names TBD; align with existing router namespace conventions):
- router_fallback_activated_total{region, route, customer_tier, requested_model, served_model, reason}
  - Increment once per request when the served target differs from requested due to a fallback decision.
  - requested_model/served_model should be normalized identifiers (e.g., catalog slug), not full internal build IDs.
- router_fallback_requests_total{region, route, customer_tier, requested_model}
  - Increment once per request where fallback was eligible (denominator for rate).
- router_fallback_ineligible_total{region, route, customer_tier, requested_model, reason}
  - Helps distinguish “fallback not happening” vs “fallback impossible.”

Reason enum proposal (finalize with Routing + SRE):
- capacity_exhausted
- upstream_model_unhealthy
- upstream_region_degraded
- policy_forced (manual mitigation / config toggle)
- version_unavailable (requested version not present in region/pool)
- compatibility_mismatch (quant/profile/hardware constraints)
- safety_block (request rejected by policy; if applicable—confirm whether this is handled pre-router)

Notes:
- If we already have a single “decision” metric, prefer extending it rather than adding parallel metrics, as long as semantics remain clear. The key requirement is a direct “fallback activated” signal.
- Avoid labels that explode cardinality: do not include organization/workspace IDs. Use customer_tier only (self_serve/dedicated/private/enterprise).
- requested_model/served_model should be bounded to the catalog + known fallbacks; still monitor cardinality in prod.
- Tie-in with SUP-1847 (customer belief that model version pin was bypassed). This metric should allow Support to confirm whether fallback occurred and whether reason was version_unavailable vs policy_forced.

Dashboards:
- Add to Support-safe dashboard folder (view-only permissions).
- Panels:
  1) Fallback activation rate (activated_total / requests_total) by region (last 1h/24h).
  2) Top fallback reasons (stacked) by region.
  3) Requested vs served model (top transitions) for a selected route (limited to top-N to keep readable).

Runbook snippet (owned by SRE + Support Enablement):
- “If fallback activation rate >X% and reason is upstream_region_degraded or upstream_model_unhealthy, move to #incidents and page SRE per playbook.”
- “If reason is version_unavailable/compatibility_mismatch and limited to one tier/route, page Platform Routing on-call after Support collects required fields.”
rollout_plan:
1) Implement metrics behind a feature flag (router_metrics_fallback_v2).
2) Validate in staging with forced fallback scenarios:
   - simulate capacity_exhausted
   - simulate upstream_model_unhealthy
   - simulate policy_forced
3) Canary enable in one low-risk production region for 24 hours; watch metrics volume/cardinality.
4) Enable globally.
5) Add dashboards + link from Support escalation playbook/runbook.

Rollback: disable feature flag; metrics should stop emitting without impacting routing behavior.
comments: 2026-02-06 (Mina Haddad): Filed from Support feedback during known-issues sprint. We need a single metric Support can point at during a bridge: “fallback is happening now” + “reason.”

2026-02-07 (Allison Grant): Agree. Main risk is label cardinality (requested_model/served_model). We can normalize to catalog slug + cap panels to top-N. Will add a metrics review step before global enable.

2026-02-10 (Rafael Mendes): Please ensure reason taxonomy matches how we actually decide fallback. Also: do NOT add anything that implies paging thresholds; Support can use it for triage but we page on SLO symptoms (error rate/latency) per policy.
2026-02-12 (Priya Shah): Support request: dashboard needs an obvious yes/no read. A simple single-stat panel like “Fallback active in last 5m (by region)” would help on bridges.

2026-02-16 (Allison Grant): Started implementation. Drafted enum reasons; need routing team confirmation on safety_block vs rejected earlier in gateway. Will post a short proposal in #eng-platform for sign-off.
